title: Kuk Early Agricultural Site
summary: Kuk Swamp, in the upper Wahgi Valley of the Papua New Guinea highlands, preserves traces of cultivation from about 10,000 calendar years ago, with mounded plots and drainage ditches from about 7,000–6,400 years ago. It is a key site for independent agricultural development in New Guinea, though researchers disagree about when true agriculture began.

uncertainty.note: Year numbers are cal BP converted with year = 1950 − cal BP. Whether Phase 1 is agriculture is disputed. Use of the swamp continues in later phases, not shown here.

as_recorded.value: c. 10,000 cal. BP amorphous palaeosurface (Phase 1); 6950–6440 cal. BP mounded palaeosurface (Phase 2)

where.modern_name: Kuk Swamp, about 12–13 km northeast of Mount Hagen, Western Highlands, Papua New Guinea
where.historical_name: Kuk Swamp, upper Wahgi Valley, New Guinea highlands (about 1,550 m altitude); no polities at this date

importance.justification: A rare site with evidence of independent early cultivation in New Guinea, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site (WHC 887, not opened here).

sources.title: Ten Thousand Years of Cultivation at Kuk Swamp in the Highlands of Papua New Guinea, ch. 1
sources.author: Jack Golson et al.

sources.title: Swamp cultivators at Kuk, New Guinea (The Cambridge World History)

reviewer_note: UNESCO pages (WHC 887) returned 403, so the inscription and exact site coordinates are unconfirmed; the pin is the Mount Hagen town point from GeoNames, with the ANU "12–13 km northeast" offset noted only in uncertainty_km (20). A refinement is needed from UNESCO. Earlier reports of ditches about 9,000 BP are not used.
